record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: Let phi: R^d -> R be a nonnegative integrable convolution kernel with integral 1, let phi_t(x) = t^{-d} phi(x/t), and define M_phi f(x) = sup_{t>0} (phi_t * |f|)(x). For a real-valued function f on R of bounded variation, can one prove Var(M_phi f) <= C(phi) Var(f)? For which kernels phi can one prove the sharp version with C(phi)=1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a nonnegative integrable kernel with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\varphi(x)\,dx=1$. For $t>0$ define the dilation $\varphi_t(x)=t^{-d}\varphi(x/t)$, and define the convolution maximal operator
$$M_\varphi f(x)=\sup_{t>0}\,(\varphi_t*|f|)(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For a real-valued function $f$ of bounded variation on $\mathbb{R}$ (the case $d=1$), let $\operatorname{Var}(f)$ denote its total variation on $\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C(\varphi)<\infty$, depending only on $\varphi$, such that
$$\operatorname{Var}(M_\varphi f)\le C(\varphi)\,\operatorname{Var}(f)$$
for every $f\in BV(\mathbb{R})$.

(b) Identify the class of kernels $\varphi$ for which the sharp inequality holds with constant $C(\varphi)=1$, i.e.
$$\operatorname{Var}(M_\varphi f)\le \operatorname{Var}(f)\qquad\text{for all }f\in BV(\mathbb{R}).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The variation-bounding property for convolution maximal operators has been established for specific smooth kernels (e.g., Gauss and Poisson kernels) by Carneiro and Svaiter, and follow-up work by Carneiro–Madrid and others. However, the general questions of (i) proving the bound for arbitrary nonnegative integrable kernels and (ii) classifying kernels achieving sharp constant 1 remain open, as posed in surveys on regularity of maximal operators.

status_evidence.title: On the variation of maximal operators of convolution type II
status_evidence.snippet: Carneiro and Madrid study variation bounds for maximal operators associated to smooth convolution kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist only for specific smooth kernels; the general kernel case remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the variation of maximal operators of convolution type
status_evidence.snippet: Carneiro and Svaiter establish variation-diminishing properties for maximal operators associated to the heat and Poisson kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp constant C(phi)=1 is known for special kernels (heat, Poisson) but not classified in general.
